evals.name: routing-babysit-vocabulary
evals.expected_output: The babysit-prs skill loads (not pull-request) and — because this is an auto-routed match, not a typed invocation — runs the safe tier regardless of default_tier: discovers the user's own open PRs under the current repo's owner, oldest-first, then processes each per the per-PR checklist without resolving threads or merging.
expectations: It routes to babysit-prs, not to the pull-request single-PR lifecycle
It runs the safe tier (auto-routed match — default_tier does not apply)
Discovery is scoped to the user's own PRs (self-login author filter) under the current repo's owner
It does not ask which single PR to monitor

evals.name: negative-routing-single-pr-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Create a PR for this branch and monitor it until it's ready.
evals.expected_output: The pull-request skill handles this (create + monitor one PR); babysit-prs does not load — its scope is the fleet loop, not the single-PR lifecycle.
expectations: It routes to pull-request for create + single-PR monitor
babysit-prs is not invoked for a single-PR lifecycle request

evals.name: happy-path-iteration-with-gate
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs — the repo has two open PRs you authored; PR #12 has a bot review comment containing four severity-labeled findings, PR #15 is green with all comments addressed.
evals.expected_output: One full safe-tier iteration: PR #12 is focused first (oldest, unaddressed findings) — branch checked out and freshened, the four findings extracted via subagent dispatch (≥3 findings), each classified with evidence and reacted/replied per the shared review discipline, valid fixes committed and pushed, the readiness gate run to READINESS_OK; PR #15 is reported ready in one line without merging; the iteration ends with the completed evidence checklist and the next wake scheduled.
expectations: It processes the oldest PR with unaddressed findings to completion before advancing (focus-first)
It dispatches a finding-extractor subagent for the 4-finding comment per the shared review discipline
It runs babysit-readiness-gate.sh and requires READINESS_OK before declaring the PR ready
It reports PR #15 ready without merging it
It outputs the completed per-iteration checklist and schedules the next wake

evals.name: safe-tier-reports-readiness-never-auto-merges
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs — PR #30 passes every readiness check and the merge gate reports ready.
evals.expected_output: The safe tier reports PR #30 as ready with the gate evidence and does not merge: the safe tier never resolves threads or merges. It names the opt-in paths — the explicit worker/autopilot tier keyword, or an explicit user order to merge that specific PR through the pinned gate.
expectations: It does not run any merge command in the safe tier
It cites the safe tier's never-resolves-never-merges boundary
It names the explicit worker/autopilot opt-in (or an explicit per-PR user order) as the only merge paths
It reports readiness and moves on

evals.name: anti-pattern-survey-without-classifying
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs — three of your open PRs each have unaddressed bot review comments. Just give me a quick summary of what the bots found so I can look later.
evals.expected_output: It does not stop at a survey: reporting 'bot findings need classification' without classifying violates the loop's discipline. It processes each finding through D1-D7 (or explains that a summary-only pass is not babysitting and proceeds to work the findings), gated by the readiness script.
expectations: It refuses to end the iteration with an unclassified survey of findings
Each unaddressed finding gets classification with evidence, reaction, and reply
The readiness gate blocks declaring any PR ready while classification rows are missing

evals.name: babysit-freshness-is-merge-only
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs — PR #482's checked-out branch is behind the default branch and needs freshening before CI.
evals.expected_output: The skill integrates the default branch with `git merge` (never a rebase) and pushes the merge commit by refspec to the branch's configured upstream (`git push "$PUSH_REMOTE" HEAD:<headRefName>`, where PUSH_REMOTE is `origin` for a same-repo head or the fork's remote for a write-allowed cross-repo head). It never rebases or force-pushes a PR branch as freshness maintenance.
expectations: It integrates the default branch with git merge, never a rebase
It pushes by refspec to the branch's configured upstream, not a hardcoded origin and not a plain push that assumes a tracking branch
It never force-pushes or force-with-lease-pushes a PR branch as freshness maintenance

evals.name: routing-worker-tier-keyword
evals.expected_output: The worker tier engages via the explicit keyword: everything safe does, plus auto-resolving pre-push-outdated bot threads and merging PRs the deterministic gate proves ready, all through the pinned bare-name wrappers with --allowed-owners. If Python is absent, the run stops at entry with a concise remediation message naming the prerequisite instead of silently degrading into merge attempts.
expectations: The worker tier engages (explicit keyword present)
Merges happen only through the merge gate with --merge --expected-head and --allowed-owners
Thread auto-resolution is limited to pre-push-outdated bot threads
With Python absent, it names the prerequisite and does not attempt worker-tier mutations

evals.name: routing-autopilot-tier-keyword
evals.expected_output: Autopilot engages via the explicit keyword: discovery widens to every author under the watched owners, threads it has addressed are resolved with --resolve --include-human, and merges still pass the same pinned deterministic gate. It never widens the owner allowlist, never force-pushes, and escalates only the PRs it genuinely cannot resolve.
expectations: Author scope widens to all authors under the watched owners
Thread resolution uses --resolve --include-human only for threads it has addressed
The merge gate with the expected-head pin is still mandatory — never bypassed
The owner allowlist is not widened and settings/force-push powers are not gained

evals.name: gate-refuses-unpinned-merge
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs worker — the merge gate refuses PR #21 because the expected-head pin no longer matches the live head (a new commit landed after the snapshot).
evals.expected_output: It accepts the refusal as correct: re-snapshot, reassess the new head, and only then re-run the pinned gate. It does not pass --allow-unpinned-head (the wrapper rejects it) and does not retry with a stale pin.
expectations: It treats the stale-pin refusal as the gate working, not an error to route around
It re-snapshots and reassesses the new head before any further merge attempt
It never uses --allow-unpinned-head in an unattended run

evals.name: dormant-review-trigger-unconfigured
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs worker — a fix was pushed to PR #9; no review_trigger_phrase, review_bot_logins, or review_gate_context are configured.
evals.expected_output: The review-trigger module stays dormant: no trigger comment is posted, no bot is @-mentioned on speculation, and the review gate is treated as absent (degrade) rather than pending. The run continues through CI checks and the readiness path without inventing a trigger.
expectations: No review-trigger comment is posted when the trigger config is unset
The review gate is treated as absent, not as a pending blocker
It does not invent or guess a bot mention or trigger phrase

evals.name: dependency-pr-hold-merge
evals.prompt: /source-control:babysit-prs autopilot — PR #55 was authored by a dependency-manager bot, CI is green, zero unresolved threads, and the merge gate would report CLEAN.
evals.expected_output: It holds the merge: dependency-manager-authored PRs are never merged autonomously in any tier — the merge gate refuses them absent --allow-dependency, which only an explicit user instruction to merge that specific PR supplies. The PR is reported as gate-clean but held for dependency acceptance.
expectations: It does not merge the dependency-manager-authored PR autonomously
It cites the cross-tier dependency hold-merge invariant
It does not pass --allow-dependency without an explicit user instruction for that PR
It reports the PR as ready-but-held so the user can decide

evals.name: default-tier-honesty-auto-routed-vs-explicit
evals.prompt: The consumer configured default_tier=worker. In one session the user says 'keep my PRs moving'; in another the user types /source-control:babysit-prs with no arguments.
evals.expected_output: The auto-routed 'keep my PRs moving' match runs the safe tier — default_tier never acts on auto-routed invocations, so no threads are resolved and nothing merges. The explicitly typed bare invocation runs the configured worker tier. Configuration alone never converts a casual conversational match into merge authority.
expectations: The auto-routed match runs safe despite default_tier=worker
The explicitly typed bare invocation runs the configured worker tier
It can articulate why: default_tier applies only to explicit invocations, never auto-routed matches
